note: Horse campground in Huntersville State Forest beside 24 miles of designated horse trail (two loops and a Shell River crossing). Horse sites have tie lines or picket lines, corrals, stalls and compost bins for manure; a Minnesota Horse Trail Pass is required to ride. --Claude
summary: DNR forest record (2026), forest guide (2017-18) and camping/fee pages read. The DNR never says horse sites are closed to campers without horses, but the only non-horse sites are 8 'individual campsites' inside the horse campground (2017 guide), and the 2026 record lists just 8 horse campsites: drop candidate as an indistinct horse camp. Shell City Landing Campground (19 sites) next door is not in the DB: lead. Fees note updated; phone and website changes.
flags: DROP CANDIDATE (indistinct horse camp, AWH 2026-11-09 rule): the DNR does not say non-horse campers are barred, nor that they are welcome. Its wording: camping page 'Horse campsites allow horses. In addition to the basic camping amenities provided, these sites may also have picket lines and compost bins for manure disposal. Horse camping is available by same day advance payment.'; facility record cmp00058 'The campground offers tie lines, corrals, stalls, and open space for horses.' with 'horse_campsites: 8' and no individual campsites counted; forest guide (2017-18) 'SHELL CITY HORSE CAMPGROUND ... the campground has eight individual campsites, 27 horse campsites, vault toilets, and drinking water. Horse campsites have picket lines and compost bins'. The fee page sells 'Individual and equestrian campsites' on one Yodel product. So at best 8 individual sites sit inside the horse campground with no separate non-horse loop shown anywhere, and the current DNR record shows none. The stored claim '8 general drive-in individual sites open to all campers' / 'open to everyone' is not DNR wording.

LEAD: Shell City Landing Campground (DNR cmp00027, point 46.791808,-94.948024, ~120 m W of the DNR horse-camp point) - 19 primitive campsites, vault toilets, drinking water, on the Shell River with swimming, water access and fishing, same managers, $17 FCFS same-day pay. Not in campgrounds.json (checked by name). If 5444 is dropped, this is the general campground here.
SITES conflict: stored count 35 (2017 guide: 8 individual + 27 horse) vs the 2026 DNR record's 8 horse campsites. Not changed; whichever the reviewer keeps, it is a horse camp count.
